mainTopic: Animals' items on שבת (amulets, healing, udder-pouches, לבובין), with stories in between
overview: The amud continues explaining a ברייתא about what animals may wear on שבת. The ברייתא forbids an animal's קמיע even when it is proven, so the גמרא explains that it was proven for people only, since a person's מזל helps the amulet work. The 'stricture for animals' in the ברייתא refers to the סנדל (shoe), not the amulet. The גמרא then asks whether an animal's pain counts on שבת. עולא explains that cooling a sick animal in water is forbidden because of the decree against grinding medicinal herbs. רבינא and רב נחמן בר יצחק answer a challenge to that decree, and רבא rules like רבי אושעיא, who allows healing an animal by running it. Next, two ברייתות contradict each other about a pouch on goats' udders, and the גמרא gives three ways to resolve this. Two stories follow: a father who miraculously nursed his son, and a man who never noticed that his wife was missing an arm. Finally, the גמרא returns to the משנה and gives three explanations of the word לבובין, then starts proving the meaning of שחוזות from a verse that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The earlier item is like an amulet
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes an earlier discussion: the item under discussion in the ברייתא is like a קמיע, worn for healing. It accepts this reading with 'שמע מינה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is similar to an amulet. Learn from it that this is correct.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is closing an earlier discussion that began on the previous amud. It decides that the item being discussed works like a קמיע, meaning it is worn for healing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Comparing the item to a קמיע tells us its purpose: it is worn to heal. 'שמע מינה' is the גמרא's stamp of approval, so this reading is now accepted.

keyTerms.meaning: An amulet worn for protection or healing
'Learn from it.' The point is proven

steps.confusionAlert: This line does not begin a new topic. It is the end of the discussion that came on the previous amud. The new topic starts with 'אמר מר' in the next step.

phrases.english: Similar to an amulet.
Learn from it (that this is so).
phrases.notes: This is the גמרא's way of saying the proof works.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the previous discussion on the previous amud
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The item in question is treated like a healing קמיע.

steps.title: The ברייתא bans an animal's amulet even if proven
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a line from the ברייתא: an animal may not go out with a קמיע, even one that is מומחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: Nor may an animal go out with an amulet, even if it has been proven effective.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line from the ברייתא so it can examine it. This sets up the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A 'מומחה' amulet is one that has worked several times. Normally that status allows it to be worn on שבת, because it counts as a real remedy and not as carrying a load. The ברייתא seems to say that even a proven amulet is forbidden for an animal.

keyTerms.meaning: Proven effective (an amulet that has worked repeatedly)

phrases.english: The Master said: And not with an amulet
even if it is proven effective.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new analysis of another line in the same ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An animal may not go out on שבת with a קמיע, even a proven one.

steps.title: Our משנה implies a proven amulet is allowed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא from a משנה that forbids only an unproven קמיע. That implies a proven one is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned in a משנה: One may not go out with an amulet that is not proven. This implies that a proven amulet is fine!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא with a משנה that seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה specifically forbids an amulet 'that is not proven.' From that wording we learn that a proven amulet is permitted. So why would the ברייתא forbid even a proven one?

keyTerms.meaning: 'But we learned (in a משנה).' Introduces a source that contradicts

phrases.english: But didn't we learn (in a Mishnah):
And not with an amulet that is not proven.
This implies: a proven one is fine!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ruling quoted in step 2
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ban on a proven קמיע
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה forbids only an unproven amulet, which implies a proven one is allowed. This contradicts the ברייתא.

steps.title: The ברייתא also means an unproven amulet
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is also talking about an unproven קמיע.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, it means an amulet that is not proven.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to remove the contradiction by saying the ברייתא is talking about the same case as the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the ברייתא also means an unproven amulet, then both sources agree: unproven is forbidden and proven is allowed. The trouble is that this answer clashes with the ברייתא's actual words, which the next step points out.

phrases.english: Here too, it is one that is not proven.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction from step 3
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the case (making the ברייתא refer to the same case as the משנה)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא forbids even a proven amulet
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is talking about an unproven amulet

steps.title: But the ברייתא says 'even if proven'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the previous answer, because the ברייתא clearly says 'even if it is proven.'
steps.simpleTranslation: But it explicitly teaches 'even if it is proven'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer by pointing to the exact words of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'אף על פי שהוא מומחה' cannot describe an unproven amulet. So the answer in step 4 does not fit the text.

keyTerms.meaning: It teaches (refers to the wording of a source)

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא ״אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהוּא מוּמְחֶה״ קָתָנֵי!
phrases.english: But it teaches 'even if it is proven'!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהוּא מוּמְחֶה קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given in step 4
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the ברייתא means an unproven amulet
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא's own words say the amulet is proven.

steps.title: Proven for people but not for animals
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the amulet is proven for a person but not for an animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is proven for a person, but not proven for an animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new answer: the word 'proven' in the ברייתא means proven for humans only.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This keeps the ברייתא's wording and still agrees with the משנה. The amulet is 'מומחה' in a general sense, but it has never been proven to work on animals, so it is still unproven for the animal.

phrases.english: Proven for a person
and not proven for an animal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording challenge from step 5
steps.terutzResolutionType: Making a distinction (proven for humans versus proven for animals)
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Proven' in the ברייתא means proven for humans only

steps.title: Can an amulet work for people but not animals?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether it makes sense for an amulet to work on a person but not on an animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is there really an amulet that is proven for a person but not proven for an animal?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions whether the distinction it just made is realistic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The assumption is that healing an animal should be easier than healing a person. If the amulet works on humans, it should certainly work on animals.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And is there really?' A question that doubts something is possible

phrases.english: And is there one that is proven for a person
and is not proven for an animal?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions whether the answer in step 6 is plausible
steps.kashyaTarget: The distinction between humans and animals
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An amulet that heals people should heal animals even more easily.

steps.title: A person's מזל helps the amulet work
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers yes: a person has a מזל that helps the amulet work, and an animal has none.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes. A person, who has a מזל, is helped by it. An animal, which has no מזל, is not helped by it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why an amulet can work for people and not for animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The amulet does not work alone. It works together with the person's מזל, a heavenly guardian or influence. An animal has no מזל, so an amulet proven on people tells us nothing about animals.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why an amulet's proven status does not carry over from people to animals. That is what allows the ברייתא and the משנה to fit together.

phrases.english: Yes, a person, who has a mazal —
it helps him,
an animal, which has no mazal —
it does not help it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the doubt raised in step 7
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining the reason behind the distinction
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Animals are easier to heal, so an amulet that works on people works on animals
steps.terutzMaskana: The amulet works with the help of a person's מזל, which animals lack

steps.title: Then why is this a stricture for animals?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if the rule is the same for people and animals, why does the ברייתא call it 'a stricture for animals more than for people'?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what does 'this is a stricture for an animal more than for a person' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer by pointing to another line in the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the answer just given, the rule is identical for both: proven amulets are allowed and unproven ones are forbidden. So the ברייתא's claim that animals are treated more strictly seems to have no basis.

phrases.english: If so, what is
'this is a stricture for an animal more than for a person'?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, מַאי זֶה חוֹמֶר בַּבְּהֵמָה מִבָּאָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the conclusion of steps 6 and 8 from the ברייתא's wording
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the amulet rule is the same for people and animals
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says animals are treated more strictly, but the amulet rule as explained is identical for both.

steps.title: The stricture refers to the shoe
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that 'this is a stricture' refers to the סנדל (shoe), not the קמיע.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you think it refers to the amulet? It refers to the shoe.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by changing which item the stricture line refers to. This closes the discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person may go out with a shoe on שבת, but an animal may not. That is the real 'stricture' for animals. The amulet rule stays the same for both.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Do you think?' Introduces a mistaken assumption
Shoe or sandal (here, one placed on an animal's foot)

steps.whatToRemember: An animal may not go out with an amulet unless it has been proven for animals, because an amulet proven on people relies on the person's מזל. The phrase 'stricture for animals' refers to the shoe, which a person may wear on שבת and an animal may not.

phrases.english: Do you think it refers to the amulet?
It refers to the shoe.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 9
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigning the line to a different item (it refers to the shoe, not the amulet)

steps.title: Proof from oiling and scraping a scab
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that allows oiling and scraping a scab for a person but not for an animal. It suggests this is a case of a real wound and real pain.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: We may oil and scrape a scab for a person, but we may not oil and scrape for an animal. Isn't this talking about a case where there is a wound, and it is done because of pain?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to try to prove that we do not take an animal's pain into account on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא allows oiling and scraping for a person but forbids it for an animal. The גמרא wants to read this as a case of a real wound that hurts. If so, an animal's pain would not be enough reason to allow treatment, even though a person's pain would be.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
We may smear oil and scrape a scab for a person,
but we may not smear oil and scrape for an animal.
Is it not where there is a wound,
phrases.notes: The גמרא proposes how to read the ברייתא.

phrases.english: and it is done because of pain!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new line of proof about whether an animal's pain matters on שבת.
steps.raayaObject: That an animal's pain does not allow treatment on שבת, while a person's pain does.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא: סכין ומפרכסין לאדם ואין סכין ומפרכסין לבהמה, read as a case of a wound with pain.

steps.title: The scab case is about pleasure, not pain
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. The ברייתא is speaking about a wound that has already healed, where the oiling is only for pleasure.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It is talking about a case where the wound has already healed, and it is done for pleasure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes off the proof. The ברייתא is about a healed wound, done only because it feels good.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the wound is already healed, there is no pain at all. A person's comfort is allowed, but there is no reason to do this for an animal. So the ברייתא tells us nothing about an animal that is actually in pain.

keyTerms.meaning: The wound has already finished healing

phrases.english: No, where the wound has already healed,
and it is done for pleasure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of Step 11 by giving the ברייתא a different case.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof completely by reading the ברייתא as a different case.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the ברייתא was about pain. It can just as well be about pleasure after the wound has healed.

steps.title: Proof from cooling an overheated animal in water
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא says an overheated animal may not be stood in water to cool off, but a person may.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: An animal that is suffering from too much blood (overheating) may not be stood in water to cool it off. A person suffering from too much blood may be stood in water to cool him off.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא that seems to show an animal's suffering does not matter on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the animal is truly suffering, so the 'pleasure' answer from before cannot work. Still, the ברייתא forbids cooling the animal while allowing it for a person. This seems to prove that an animal's pain is not a reason to allow treatment.

keyTerms.meaning: Seized by blood — overheated or congested, a dangerous condition
So that it will cool off

phrases.english: Come and hear:
An animal seized by blood (overheated),
we may not stand it in water
so that it will cool off.
A person seized by blood,
we may stand him in water
so that he will cool off.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof was rejected, the גמרא tries a second, stronger proof where real suffering is involved.
steps.raayaObject: That an animal's suffering does not allow treatment on שבת.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about בהמה שאחזה דם.

steps.title: עולא: a decree because of grinding herbs
steps.stepSummary: עולא explains that the animal ruling is a rabbinic decree. The worry is that the owner might come to grind herbs for medicine.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: It is a decree because of grinding medicinal herbs.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא explains the ברייתא in a different way, so it no longer proves that an animal's pain is ignored.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban is not because the animal's pain does not count. חכמים forbade medical treatment on שבת so that people would not come to grind herbs for medicine, which is a Torah-level מלאכה. Cooling the animal looks like medical treatment, so it falls under that decree.

keyTerms.meaning: Grinding herbs or ingredients for medicine

steps.confusionAlert: עולא is not saying that grinding is actually happening here. Standing the animal in water is not grinding at all. חכמים forbade it as a fence, so people would not come to grind herbs later.

phrases.english: עולא said:
It is a decree because of grinding medicinal herbs.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר עוּלָּא: גְּזֵירָה מִשּׁוּם שְׁחִיקַת סַמְמָנִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the proof of Step 13 by giving a different reason for the ban on the animal.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a different reason for the ruling (a rabbinic decree), so it is not about ignoring pain.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ban shows that an animal's suffering does not matter on שבת.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ban comes from the decree against medical treatment, made because of שחיקת סממנין.

steps.title: Then the decree should apply to a person too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges עולא: if the reason is the decree against medicine, a person should also be forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, a person too should be forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks עולא's answer. The same decree should forbid cooling a person as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The decree against medical treatment applies to people too. So why does the ברייתא allow standing a person in water? עולא's reason seems to prove too much.

keyTerms.meaning: If so — if your reasoning is right

phrases.english: If so, a person too (should be forbidden)!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges עולא's answer from Step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's reason, the decree because of שחיקת סממנין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The medicine decree applies to people as well, yet the ברייתא allows a person. So the decree cannot be the reason for forbidding the animal.

steps.title: A person looks like he is just cooling off
steps.stepSummary: A person standing in water does not look like he is getting medical treatment. It looks like he is just cooling off.
steps.simpleTranslation: A person looks like he is just cooling off.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that for a person, being in water does not look like medicine, so the decree does not apply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People often go into water just to cool down on a hot day. Nobody watching would think he is taking medicine. Since it does not look like treatment, the worry about grinding herbs does not come up.

keyTerms.meaning: Like one who is cooling off

phrases.english: A person looks like he is just cooling off.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Draws a distinction: how the act looks to others.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The medicine decree should forbid cooling a person too.
steps.terutzMaskana: For a person it looks like ordinary cooling off, not medicine, so the decree does not apply.

steps.title: Then an animal should also look like it is cooling off
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: why not say an animal in water also just looks like it is cooling off?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, an animal too should look like it is just cooling off!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the last answer. The same logic should work for an animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'it just looks like cooling off' saves the person, it should save the animal too. Then there would be no reason to forbid the animal.

phrases.english: If so, an animal too
should look like it is just cooling off!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי בְּהֵמָה נָמֵי נִרְאֶה כְּמֵיקֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 16 by applying it to an animal.
steps.kashyaTarget: The distinction נראה כמיקר from Step 16.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same appearance should apply to an animal, which would remove the reason for the ban.

steps.title: Animals are not put in water just to cool off
steps.stepSummary: Nobody stands an animal in water just to cool it off. So when it is done, it clearly looks like medical treatment.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is no 'cooling off' for an animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that animals are not normally cooled in water for comfort. So doing it clearly looks like medicine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since it is not normal to cool an animal in water for comfort, anyone watching would see it as medical treatment. That brings in the medicine decree because of שחיקת סממנין. So עולא's explanation stands, and the ברייתא does not prove that an animal's pain is ignored.

keyTerms.meaning: There is no 'cooling off' for an animal; it is not normally done

steps.whatToRemember: The ban on cooling an overheated animal is a rabbinic decree against medical treatment, made because of שחיקת סממנין. It does not prove that an animal's pain is ignored. A person is allowed because for him it looks like normal cooling off. For an animal it does not, so it looks like medicine.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common pattern in הלכות שבת: the same act can be allowed or forbidden depending on how it looks, normal comfort or medical treatment.

phrases.english: There is no 'cooling off' for an animal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 17 and keeps עולא's explanation in place.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Draws a distinction based on what people normally do.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: An animal in water could also look like it is just cooling off.
steps.terutzMaskana: Animals are not normally cooled for comfort, so it looks like medicine and the decree applies.

steps.title: Do the Sages really make decrees for animals?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges עולא with a ברייתא: an owner may call his animal back from outside the תחום, and we do not worry that he will go out and bring it himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do we really make a decree for an animal? A ברייתא teaches: if an animal was standing outside the תחום, the owner may call it and it comes to him. We do not decree that calling is forbidden out of fear that he will go out and bring it himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks עולא's answer from step 14. It brings a ברייתא where the רבנן did NOT make a decree for an animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא there was a real risk: the owner might walk out past the תחום to get his animal. Even so, the רבנן did not forbid calling it. So why would they forbid standing an animal in water just because the owner might grind herbs?

keyTerms.meaning: The שבת boundary (about 2000 אמות) you may not walk past
He calls it and it comes by itself
Perhaps / lest (the worry behind a decree)

phrases.english: And for an animal, do we make a decree?
But wasn't it taught in a ברייתא:
If it was standing outside the Shabbat limit,
he may call it and it comes.
And we do not decree, lest he come to bring it himself.
phrases.notes: The ברייתא shows no decree was made even though there was a real risk.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending why only an animal is forbidden (step 18), the גמרא now questions whether the רבנן make decrees for animals at all.
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's claim that the animal-in-water rule is a decree lest one grind herbs
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא shows the רבנן did not decree about an animal even when the owner might come to break a real prohibition, so they should not decree here either.

steps.title: רבינא: the animal's limit was inside the owner's limit
steps.stepSummary: רבינא says the ברייתא is a special case. The animal left its own תחום but is still within the owner's תחום, so there is nothing to fear.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: The case is where the animal's תחום was swallowed up inside the owner's תחום.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא pushes back on the proof. He explains that in the ברייתא's case the owner would not break any rule even if he went to get the animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal's תחום follows its shepherd, but the owner's תחום can reach farther. If the animal is past its own תחום but still inside the owner's, the owner may walk there. So there is nothing to decree about, and the ברייתא tells us nothing about decrees for animals.

keyTerms.meaning: For example / the case is where

steps.confusionAlert: The animal really is outside ITS OWN תחום. It is only the owner's larger תחום that makes this case safe.

phrases.english: Ravina said:
The case is where its limit
was contained within his limit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 19 by narrowing the ברייתא's case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא proves the רבנן never decree about animals.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is a case with no possible violation, so it says nothing against עולא's decree.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק: this is a dispute between תנאים
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers differently: whether the decree about grinding herbs applies to animals is itself argued by תנאים, as seen in the case of an animal that ate vetch.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: The decree about grinding herbs (for an animal) is itself a dispute between תנאים. A ברייתא teaches: if an animal ate vetch, one may not run it around the yard to heal it. But רבי אושעיא permits it.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a second, different way to handle the challenge. Instead of reinterpreting the ברייתא, רב נחמן בר יצחק says the question depends on a disagreement between תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion forbids running a sick animal to heal it, which means they hold healing animals is under the decree. רבי אושעיא permits it, so he holds there is no such decree for animals. So the ברייתא from step 19 may follow רבי אושעיא, and עולא's decree may follow the first opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a dispute between תנאים
Vetch, a type of animal feed that can cause harmful bloating
So that it will be healed

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
The decree about grinding herbs is itself a dispute between Tannaim.
As it was taught in a ברייתא:
An animal that ate vetch
one may not run it around in the courtyard
in order that it be healed,
and Rabbi Oshaya permits it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר: שְׁחִיקַת סַמְמָנִין גּוּפָה תַּנָּאֵי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer to step 19 than רבינא did.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Everyone agrees on whether the רבנן decree about animals, so the ברייתא contradicts עולא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The issue is argued by תנאים, so עולא and the ברייתא simply follow different opinions.

steps.title: רבא rules like רבי אושעיא
steps.stepSummary: רבא taught publicly that the הלכה follows רבי אושעיא, who permits healing an animal in this way.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא taught: The הלכה is like רבי אושעיא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds the practical ruling. רבא decides the dispute from the last step in favor of רבי אושעיא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רבי אושעיא permits running the animal to heal it, the הלכה is that the decree against healing does not apply to animals in this case. This closes the section about animals and healing.
steps.whatToRemember: There is a dispute between תנאים whether the decree against healing applies to animals. רבא rules like רבי אושעיא, who is lenient.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives the practical bottom line: healing an animal by running it is permitted, against the strict view behind עולא's explanation.

phrases.english: Rava taught publicly:
The halacha is in accordance with Rabbi Oshaya.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides the dispute brought by רב נחמן בר יצחק.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows רבי אושעיא: one may run an animal that ate vetch to heal it.

steps.title: Quoting a ברייתא: no pouch for a זב or for goats
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the ברייתא it was explaining and quotes a new line: a זב may not go out with his pouch, and goats may not go out with the pouch on their udders.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said (in the ברייתא): A זב may not go out with his pouch, and goats may not go out with the pouch on their udders.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the ברייתא it has been studying. This line is being quoted to set up the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A זב wears a pouch to catch his discharge, and goats wear a pouch on their udders. This ברייתא says neither may go out with it on שבת. The next step will show another ברייתא that seems to say the opposite about goats.

keyTerms.meaning: A man with a type of impure discharge

phrases.english: The Master said:
A zav may not go out with his pouch,
nor goats with the pouch that is on their udders.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: לֹא יֵצֵא הַזָּב בַּכִּיס שֶׁלּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of healing animals and goes back to another line of the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A זב may not go out with his pouch, and goats may not go out with an udder-pouch.

steps.title: Another ברייתא says goats may go out with the udder-pouch
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out a contradiction: a different ברייתא says goats MAY go out with the pouch on their udders.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a ברייתא teaches: Goats may go out with the pouch on their udders!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that two ברייתות disagree about goats with udder-pouches. It is setting up a question that will need an answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 23 said goats may not go out with the pouch. This ברייתא says they may. The גמרא must find a way to explain both.
steps.confusionAlert: Both sources are about goats with the same pouch. One says forbidden and one says permitted. That clash is the whole question.

phrases.english: But wasn't it taught in a ברייתא:
Goats may go out with the pouch that is on their udders!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling just quoted in step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ruling that goats may not go out with an udder-pouch
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another ברייתא directly permits the same thing, so the two sources contradict each other.

steps.title: Tight pouch versus loose pouch
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה resolves the contradiction. A pouch tied tightly is permitted, and a loosely tied pouch is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: This is not difficult. This ברייתא, which permits, is talking about a pouch that is tied tightly. That ברייתא, which forbids, is talking about a pouch that is not tied tightly.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers the contradiction from Step 24 by saying the two ברייתות are talking about two different situations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A tightly tied pouch will not fall off, so there is no worry that the owner will pick it up and carry it in the street. A loose pouch might fall off, and the owner might carry it. That is why it is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; the two sources do not really contradict
This one ... that one; used to split two sources into two cases

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said: It is not difficult:
this one is where it is tied tightly,
phrases.notes: The permitting ברייתא. It will not fall off.

phrases.english: that one is where it is not tied tightly.
phrases.notes: The forbidding ברייתא. It may fall, and the owner may carry it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in Step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the two sources into two different cases (אוקימתא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both ברייתות seemed to be talking about the same pouch, so they seemed to contradict.
steps.terutzMaskana: The permitting ברייתא is about a tightly tied pouch, and the forbidding ברייתא is about a loose one.

steps.title: It is a dispute between the תנאים
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says there is no need to invent a split. The two ברייתות reflect a known dispute among תנאים in the משנה about goats with bound udders.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Have you removed the תנאים from the world? This is a dispute between תנאים, as we learned in the משנה: Goats may go out with their udders bound. רבי יוסי forbids all of these items, except for the ewes that are כבונות. רבי יהודה says: Goats may go out with their udders bound to dry up their milk, but not to save their milk.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives a different answer. The two ברייתות simply follow different תנאים, and he proves this by quoting the משנה, where תנאים disagree about bound udders.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף's opening line is a gentle rebuke: why force the two ברייתות into different cases when we already know תנאים argue about this exact topic? The משנה shows three views. The first opinion permits, רבי יוסי forbids almost everything, and רבי יהודה permits only when the binding is done to dry up the milk. So one ברייתא follows a permitting view, and the other follows a forbidding view.

keyTerms.meaning: Have you removed the תנאים from the world? Meaning: why ignore that this is simply a dispute among תנאים?
It is a dispute among תנאים
Bound; here, goats whose udders are tied up
Ewes wrapped in a cloth to keep their wool clean
To dry up the milk, so the goat stops nursing and can become pregnant
To save the milk, so it does not drip out

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up רב יהודה, the אמורא in Step 25, with רבי יהודה, the תנא quoted in the משנה here. They are two different people from different eras.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a basic גמרא strategy. Instead of forcing two sources to agree, you may say they follow different תנאים.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
Have you removed the tanna'im from the world?
phrases.notes: He isn't really asking. He's scolding the forced split in Step 25.

phrases.english: It is a dispute of tanna'im, as we learned in the mishna:
Goats may go out with udders bound,
Rabbi Yosei forbids all of them,
phrases.notes: He treats these items as burdens.

phrases.english: except for the ewes that are wrapped,
Rabbi Yehuda says:
Goats may go out bound to dry up the milk,
phrases.notes: Here the binding is tight and permanent.

phrases.english: but not to save the milk.
phrases.notes: Here the binding is loose and may fall off.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer to the contradiction instead of רב יהודה's split.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the sources to different תנאים (תנאי היא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed both ברייתות must follow one opinion, so we had to find different cases.
steps.terutzMaskana: The two ברייתות follow different תנאים who disagree about bound udders, as seen in the משנה.

steps.title: Both follow רבי יהודה: drying versus saving milk
steps.stepSummary: A third answer says both ברייתות follow רבי יהודה. The permitting one is about binding to dry up the milk, and the forbidding one is about binding to save the milk.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say: both this ברייתא and that ברייתא follow רבי יהודה, and it is not difficult. Here, it is about drying up the milk. There, it is about saving the milk.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers another way to answer the contradiction. Both ברייתות can follow a single תנא, רבי יהודה, using the distinction he himself made in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer keeps both ברייתות inside רבי יהודה's view. Binding to dry up the milk is done tightly and permanently, so it is permitted. Binding to save the milk is done loosely, so it is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say; introduces an alternative answer
This one and that one; both sources
Here ... there; splits two sources into two cases

steps.whatToRemember: There are three answers to the pouch contradiction. First, tight versus loose. Second, a dispute between תנאים. Third, both follow רבי יהודה, and it depends on whether the binding is to dry up the milk or to save it.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
this one and that one follow Rabbi Yehuda,
and it is not difficult:
here it is to dry up the milk, there it is to save the milk.
phrases.notes: Drying up is permitted. Saving the milk is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: הָא וְהָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the משנה quoted in Step 26 to give a different answer, in which both ברייתות follow one תנא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases within a single opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Following רב יוסף, the two ברייתות would need two different תנאים.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both follow רבי יהודה. Binding to dry up the milk is permitted, and binding to save the milk is forbidden.

steps.title: The goats of אנטוכיא with large udders
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records רבי יהודה's story about goats in אנטוכיא whose udders were so large that people made pouches for them so the udders would not get scratched.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: רבי יהודה said: There was an incident with the goats of אנטוכיא, whose udders were large. People made pouches for them so that their udders would not get scratched.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with a story from רבי יהודה. It shows another reason people put pouches on goats' udders: to protect them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far we have seen two purposes for binding udders: to dry up the milk and to save the milk. This story adds a third purpose, protecting very large udders from scratches as they drag along the ground. In that case, the pouch works as protection for the animal.

keyTerms.meaning: An incident or story, used to teach a law from real life

phrases.english: It was taught in a baraita: Rabbi Yehuda said:
There was an incident with the goats of Antioch
whose udders were large,
phrases.notes: They would drag along the ground.

phrases.english: and they made pouches for them
so that their udders would not get scratched.
phrases.notes: A third purpose for the pouch: protection.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּעִזִּים שֶׁל אַנְטוֹכְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a related ברייתא from רבי יהודה about another reason for pouches on goats' udders.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Pouches were placed on the large udders of the goats of אנטוכיא to protect them from scratches.

steps.title: A father miraculously nurses his son
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא tells of a widower who could not afford a wet-nurse, and a miracle let him nurse his baby himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: There was a man whose wife died and left him a nursing baby. He had no money to pay a wet-nurse. A miracle happened: he grew breasts like a woman's and nursed his son.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא, a story about a man who grew breasts by a miracle so he could nurse his baby. It follows the previous story about goats' oversized udders.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The link to the sugya is the topic of udders and breasts. This is not a new halachic ruling. It is a story that sets up the discussion of the next few steps about what such a miracle means.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
There was an incident with one man whose wife died
and she left behind a son who still needed to nurse

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא הָיָה לוֹ שְׂכַר מְנִיקָה לִיתֵּן,
phrases.english: and he did not have money to pay a wet-nurse's wages,
and a miracle was done for him

phrases.aramaic: וְנִפְתְּחוּ לוֹ דַּדִּין כִּשְׁנֵי דַּדֵּי אִשָּׁה
phrases.english: and he developed breasts like a woman's two breasts
and he nursed his son.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּאֶחָד שֶׁמֵּתָה אִשְׁתּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Associative continuation: from goats' large udders to a man who miraculously grew breasts.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A miracle allowed a poor widower to nurse his own infant son.

steps.title: The man must have been very great
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says the miracle shows how great this man was.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Come and see how great this man was, that such a miracle was done for him!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives his reading of the story: the man must have been very righteous to deserve such a miracle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף reasons that miracles are done for people of merit, so a miracle this big shows great merit. This sets up אביי's opposite reading in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and see (opens a lesson drawn from a story)

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:

phrases.aramaic: בֹּא וּרְאֵה כַּמָּה גָּדוֹל אָדָם זֶה
phrases.english: Come and see how great this man is
that a miracle like this was done for him!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: בֹּא וּרְאֵה כַּמָּה גָּדוֹל אָדָם זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a lesson from the story in step 29.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A great miracle shows the person's great merit.

steps.title: On the contrary, the man was lowly
steps.stepSummary: אביי turns רב יוסף's reading upside down: changing nature for him shows he was lacking.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: On the contrary! How lowly this man was, that the natural order of creation had to be changed for him.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי rejects רב יוסף's praise and argues that the story actually reflects poorly on the man.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי agrees that a miracle happened. He objects to the kind of miracle. If the man had real merit, he could have been helped in a normal way, such as being given money. Instead nature was changed, and in an undignified way, since a man had to become like a woman.

keyTerms.meaning: On the contrary (flips the previous claim)

steps.confusionAlert: אביי does not deny the miracle. He only disputes what it says about the man.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
On the contrary, how lowly this man is
that the order of creation was changed for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב יוסף's reading of the story by reversing it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רב יוסף's conclusion that the miracle shows greatness.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Changing nature, especially in a demeaning way, shows a lack of merit, not an abundance of it.

steps.title: How hard it is to provide a person's food
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה learns from the story that providing a person's food is so hard that nature itself had to change.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: Come and see how hard a person's food is to provide, that the order of creation was changed for him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה draws a different lesson from the same story, this time about how hard it is to earn a living.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Changing the man's body was apparently easier than simply giving him money for food. This shows how difficult a person's sustenance is, even in Heaven's eyes.

keyTerms.meaning: Food, a person's sustenance or livelihood

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:

phrases.aramaic: בֹּא וּרְאֵה כַּמָּה קָשִׁים מְזוֹנוֹתָיו שֶׁל אָדָם,
phrases.english: Come and see how difficult a person's sustenance is,
that the order of creation was changed on his account.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: בֹּא וּרְאֵה כַּמָּה קָשִׁים מְזוֹנוֹתָיו שֶׁל אָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new lesson from the same story, separate from the רב יוסף and אביי debate.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person's sustenance is so hard to provide that nature was changed rather than providing it directly.

steps.title: Proof: miracles happen, but food is never created
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן supports רב יהודה: miracles do happen, yet food is never miraculously created.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: Know that this is true, for miracles do happen, but food has never been created.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן brings support for רב יהודה's point using a general observation about miracles.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Many kinds of miracles occur, yet Heaven does not simply create food in a person's house. This confirms that sustenance is an especially hard thing to grant, which backs up רב יהודה's reading of the story.
steps.whatToRemember: From the nursing-father story: רב יוסף sees greatness, אביי sees lowliness (nature was changed), and רב יהודה with רב נחמן learn how hard it is to provide a person's food.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said: Know that it is so,
for miracles do happen
but food has not been created.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב יהודה's lesson in step 32.
steps.raayaObject: רב יהודה's claim that sustenance is very hard to provide.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The observation that miracles occur but food is never miraculously created.

steps.title: A man never noticed his wife was missing an arm
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא tells of a man who married a woman missing a hand or arm and never noticed until she died.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: There was a man who married a woman missing an arm, and he did not notice it until the day she died.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another unusual story. It sets up the debate in the next two steps about who deserves the praise for modesty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new detail is that a full marriage passed without the husband discovering his wife's physical defect. The question that follows is whose conduct made this possible.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman missing a hand or arm

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:

phrases.aramaic: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּאָדָם אֶחָד שֶׁנָּשָׂא אִשָּׁה גִּידֶּמֶת
phrases.english: There was an incident with a man who married a one-armed woman

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא הִכִּיר בָּהּ עַד יוֹם מוֹתָהּ.
phrases.english: and he did not notice it until the day of her death.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּאָדָם אֶחָד שֶׁנָּשָׂא אִשָּׁה גִּידֶּמֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another unusual story, following the previous one.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A husband did not notice his wife's missing arm for their entire marriage.

steps.title: The wife must have been very modest
steps.stepSummary: רב praises the wife's modesty for keeping her defect hidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: Come and see how modest this woman was, that her husband never noticed.
steps.whatsHappening: רב explains the story by crediting the wife: she was so modestly covered that her husband never saw her defect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב reads the story as praise of the woman's צניעות. This sets up רבי חייא's challenge in the next step.

phrases.english: Rav said:

phrases.aramaic: בֹּא וּרְאֵה כַּמָּה צְנוּעָה אִשָּׁה זוֹ
phrases.english: Come and see how modest this woman was
that her husband did not notice it about her.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: בֹּא וּרְאֵה כַּמָּה צְנוּעָה אִשָּׁה זוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a lesson from the story in step 34.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The wife's modesty kept her defect hidden.

steps.title: No, the husband was the modest one
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא says hiding a defect is natural for a woman, so the real praise belongs to the husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא said to him: That is simply her natural way. Rather, say: How modest this man was, that he did not notice this in his wife.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא rejects רב's praise of the wife and moves the praise to the husband.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A woman normally covers herself, and one with a defect would surely hide it, so her behavior is not remarkable. The remarkable part is that the husband never looked closely enough at his wife to notice. That shows his great modesty.
steps.whatToRemember: In the one-armed wife story, רב praises the wife's modesty, while רבי חייא says hiding a defect is natural for her, and the real praise goes to the husband who never looked.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiya said to him:
This is her normal way.
Rather, say: how modest this man was
that he did not notice it in his wife.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי חִיָּיא: זוֹ דַּרְכָּהּ בְּכָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב's reading and replaces it with a new one.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רב's claim that the story praises the wife.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Hiding a defect is normal behavior for a woman, so it is not special praise. The unusual conduct is the husband's.

steps.title: What does 'לבובין' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה's phrase 'rams go out לבובין' and asks what the word means.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: Rams may go out לבובין. What does לבובין mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The story is finished, and the גמרא goes back to the משנה. It quotes the words 'rams go out לבובין' and asks what that unusual word means. This sets up the answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists things an animal may wear on שבת, but the word לבובין is unclear. Before we can know what is allowed, we need to know what object the משנה is describing. Three different explanations will follow.

keyTerms.meaning: The unclear word in the משנה that is being defined

steps.confusionAlert: This is not part of the earlier story. The גמרא has gone back to explaining the words of the משנה about animals on שבת.

phrases.english: Rams may go out levuvin.
What is 'levuvin'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the אגדה to explaining the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the word לבובין in the משנה

steps.title: רב הונא: rams tied in pairs
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא explains that לבובין means 'tied together', meaning the rams are tied in pairs.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: It means tied (in pairs).
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא gives the first answer. לבובין means the rams go out tied to one another in pairs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רב הונא's view, לבובין describes how the rams are tied together, not a special item they wear. This is the first of three explanations of the word.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said: Tied (in pairs).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 37
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: לבובין means the rams are tied in pairs

steps.title: Where do we see that 'לבובין' means closeness?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we know that לבובין is a word that means bringing close.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where can we tell that this word לבובין is a word for closeness?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a source for רב הונא's reading. It wants to know how we can tell that לבובין means being close or joined together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Tying rams in pairs means bringing them close to each other. The גמרא wants language proof that the root of לבובין carries this meaning of closeness.

keyTerms.meaning: From where is it implied? How do we see this?
A word that means bringing close

phrases.english: From where may it be inferred that this word 'levuvin'
is a term of closeness?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי מַשְׁמַע דְּהַאי ״לְבוּבִין״ לִישָּׁנָא דְּקָרוֹבֵי הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the textual basis of רב הונא's definition
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A verse showing that לבב means closeness

steps.title: Proof from Song of Songs
steps.stepSummary: The verse 'לבבתני אחותי כלה' ('you have drawn me near, my sister my bride') shows that the root means closeness.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'You have drawn me near, my sister, my bride' (שיר השירים 4:9).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a verse from שיר השירים. There, the same root (לבב) means 'you drew me close'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since לבבתני uses the same root as לבובין and means drawing near, the word in the משנה can mean rams joined closely together. This supports רב הונא's explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: You have drawn me near (from the root לבב)

phrases.english: As it is written: 'You have drawn me near, my sister, my bride.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 39 with a verse
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The verse לבבתני shows that the root לבב means closeness

steps.title: עולא: a hide over the heart against wolves
steps.stepSummary: עולא explains that לבובין is a piece of hide tied over the rams' hearts to protect them from wolves.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: It is a hide that is tied on them over their heart, so that wolves will not attack them.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא gives a second, different explanation. לבובין is a piece of leather tied over the heart (לב) of each ram to protect it from wolves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא connects לבובין to the word לב (heart) instead of to closeness. In his view, the משנה is talking about a protective item the ram wears. This raises a question the גמרא will now press: why would only rams need it?

phrases.english: Ulla said:
A hide that one ties on them over their heart,
so that wolves will not attack them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, competing definition of לבובין
steps.mimraCoreRuling: לבובין is a protective hide over the heart against wolves

steps.title: Do wolves attack only rams?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges עולא: do wolves attack only males and leave the females alone?
steps.simpleTranslation: Wolves attack rams, but they don't attack ewes?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges עולא. If the hide protects against wolves, why does the משנה mention it only for rams? Wolves attack ewes too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא's reading needs a reason why only males would need this protection. Without a reason, his explanation seems hard to accept.

phrases.english: Wolves attack the rams,
but they don't attack the ewes?

steps.triggerLanguage: זְאֵבִים — אַזְּכָרִים נָפְלִי, אַנְּקֵיבוֹת לָא נָפְלִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks עולא's definition
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's claim that the hide is against wolves
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Wolves threaten both males and females, so why would the protection be only for males?

steps.title: Rams walk at the front of the flock
steps.stepSummary: Answer: the rams walk at the head of the flock, so they face the wolves first.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because they walk at the head of the flock.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends עולא. Rams lead the flock, so they are the ones exposed to wolves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer claims the rams' position at the front makes them the main target. It explains why only they would need protection.

phrases.english: Because they walk at the head of the flock.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 42
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Wolves attack males and females equally
steps.terutzMaskana: Rams lead the flock, so they are attacked

steps.title: Don't wolves attack the rear too?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: do wolves attack only the front of the flock and never the back?
steps.simpleTranslation: Do wolves attack the head of the flock but not the end of the flock?
steps.whatsHappening: The answer is challenged. Wolves can attack from behind just as easily, so walking in front does not explain anything.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being in front is not a real reason a wolf would choose one sheep over another. So the previous answer falls.

phrases.english: And wolves attack at the head of the flock,
but at the end of the flock they don't attack?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּזְאֵבִין — בְּרֵישׁ עֶדְרָא נָפְלִי, בְּסוֹף עֶדְרָא לָא נָפְלִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer of step 43
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that walking in front is the reason
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Wolves attack the rear as well, so position is no reason

steps.title: Because rams are fat
steps.stepSummary: New answer: wolves go after the rams because they are plump.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is because they are fat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the first answer (אלא) and gives a new one. Wolves prefer the rams because rams are fatter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אלא shows the earlier reason has been abandoned. The new reason is that a fatter animal is more tempting to the wolves.

phrases.english: Rather: because they are fat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A replacement answer after step 44
steps.terutzMaskana: Wolves target rams because they are fatter

steps.title: Aren't some ewes fat too?
steps.stepSummary: Challenge: there are fat ewes as well.
steps.simpleTranslation: And among the ewes, aren't there fat ones?
steps.whatsHappening: The fatness answer is challenged. Some ewes are fat too, so fatness does not separate males from females.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If fatness were the reason, fat ewes would also need protection. Then the משנה should not have limited the hide to rams.

phrases.english: And among the ewes, are there none that are fat?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks step 45
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Fatness is found among females too, so it cannot explain a males-only rule

steps.title: Can wolves even tell them apart?
steps.stepSummary: A second challenge: can wolves even tell fat animals from thin ones?
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, do they know the difference between these and those?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds another problem (ותו). Wolves cannot tell which sheep are fat and which are thin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even apart from fat ewes, the fatness answer assumes wolves can judge which animals are fatter. That assumption is doubtful, so the answer falls completely.

phrases.english: And furthermore, do they know
the difference between these and those?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתוּ, מִי יָדְעִי בֵּין הָנֵי לְהָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second attack on step 45
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Wolves cannot tell fat animals from thin ones

steps.title: Rams raise their noses and look around
steps.stepSummary: Final answer: rams lift their noses and walk while looking about, so the wolves see them as a threat and attack.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is because they raise their noses and walk while looking around.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a final defense of עולא. Rams hold their heads high and look around as they walk. Wolves read this as a sign of attack and go after them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This reason is about the rams' behavior, which really is different from the ewes'. It is not about position or fatness. So עולא's view survives: only rams need the hide over their hearts.
steps.whatToRemember: עולא's explanation of לבובין (a protective hide) stands. Wolves target rams because the rams act in a way that looks aggressive.

phrases.english: Rather, because they raise their noses
and walk while looking around.
phrases.notes: The wolves think the rams are about to attack them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מִשּׁוּם דְּזָקְפִי חוּטְמַיְיהוּ וּמְסַגּוּ כִּי דָּווּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A replacement answer after steps 46-47
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Physical traits (position, fatness) explain why wolves attack
steps.terutzMaskana: The rams' bold-looking behavior draws the wolves

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק: a hide to prevent mating
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק explains that לבובין is a hide tied under the rams' male organ so they will not mount the ewes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: It is a hide tied under their male organ so that they will not mount the females.
steps.whatsHappening: A third explanation of לבובין. It is a leather covering that keeps the rams from mating with the ewes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here, too, לבובין is an item the ram wears, but its purpose is to prevent mating, not to protect against wolves. Next, רב נחמן בר יצחק will support his view from the משנה itself.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
A hide that one ties on them under their male organ,
so that they will not mount the females.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third definition of לבובין
steps.mimraCoreRuling: לבובין is a hide that prevents rams from mating

steps.title: Proof from the next clause about ewes
steps.stepSummary: The proof comes from the סיפא: ewes go out שחוזות, with tails tied up to make mating easier. So the רישא is about preventing mating, and the סיפא is about allowing it.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know this? From the later clause of the משנה: 'And ewes go out שחוזות.' What is שחוזות? Their tail is held up so that the rams can mount them. The first clause is about stopping the males from mounting the females, and the later clause is about letting the males mount them.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק proves his reading from the next line of the משנה. The ewes' item is about helping mating, so the rams' item is likely about preventing mating.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two clauses sit side by side in the משנה, so it makes sense that they deal with the same topic. In the סיפא, ewes have their tails tied up to allow mating. That fits a רישא where rams are covered to block mating, a matched pair.

keyTerms.meaning: With tails tied up (the term in the משנה)
The fatty tail of a sheep

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common method: reading one clause of a משנה in light of the clause beside it.

phrases.english: From where? From the fact that the later clause teaches:
And ewes may go out shechuzot.
What is 'shechuzot'?
That one holds their tail upward
so that the males may mount them.

phrases.aramaic: רֵישָׁא כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא יַעֲלוּ עַל הַנְּקֵבוֹת,
phrases.english: The first clause is so that they will not mount the females,
and the later clause is so that the males will mount them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 49
steps.raayaObject: רב נחמן בר יצחק's reading of לבובין
steps.raayaSupportSource: The סיפא of the משנה about ewes going out שחוזות

steps.title: Where do we see that 'שחוזות' means exposure?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we know that שחוזות is a word for uncovering.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where can we tell that this word שחוזות is a word for exposing?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a source for the meaning of שחוזות. Tying the tail up leaves the ewe uncovered, so the word should mean exposure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just as the גמרא found a verse for לבובין, it now wants language proof that שחוזות has to do with exposing.

keyTerms.meaning: A word that means exposing, uncovering

phrases.english: From where may it be inferred that this word 'shechuzot'
is a term of exposure?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי מַשְׁמַע דְּהַאי ״שְׁחוּזוֹת״ לִישָּׁנָא דְגַלּוֹיֵי הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the textual basis of the definition of שחוזות
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A verse showing that the word means exposure

steps.title: The verse begins: 'Behold a woman came toward him'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts quoting a verse from משלי about a woman dressed immodestly. This passage ends partway through the verse.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And behold, a woman came toward him...'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its answer with a verse from משלי (7:10) about an immodestly dressed woman. The verse continues on the next part of the page.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rest of the verse (בשית זונה, 'in the dress of a harlot') will show a word connected to exposure. That supports reading שחוזות as 'exposed'. Only the opening words of the verse appear on this amud; the rest comes on the next amud.

phrases.english: As it is written: 'And behold, a woman came toward him'
phrases.notes: משלי 7:10; the verse continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering step 51
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A verse from משלי about an immodestly dressed woman (continued on the next part of the page)
